the Betti numbers $\beta_\ell (\mathcal{A})$ of a pure-dimensional arrangement $\mathcal{A}$ of $n$ subspaces in $\mathbb{P}^N$ can be computed in time $\mathcal{O}^*(n^{2^{\min\{\ell, N-\ell\}}})$.

the algorithm presented in this article is the first algorithm to compute $\beta_\ell$ for an arbitrary $\ell$ in the range $0\leq\ell\leq k-2$. For $\ell=k-1$, there is an algorithm by Bajaj, Klein, Pascucci and Talmor (1996) with the same complexity bound as the algorithm presented in the article.

we show that the Betti numbers can be computed in a graded way, and that this is the best that one can hope for, in the sense that the complexity is optimal for the problem.
we show that the Betti numbers can be computed in time polynomial in $\ell$ and $n$, and independent of the ambient dimension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of computing the Berti numbers of an arrangement is determined by the complexity of computing its cohomology ring, rather than its homology ring.
the complexity of computing $\beta_\l(\cup_i S_j)$ depends on $\ell$, and not the number of sets $n$.
the complexity of computing the $\ell$-Betti number depends on $\ell$ and is independent of the number of components of the arrangement.
